Can a squatter become the owner?

Yes, but only by meeting a long list of requirements for a full ten years. West Virginia has no short squatter statute. A person who occupies land and claims title relies on adverse possession, and courts hold that person to a heavy burden of proof.

The ten years come from W. Va. Code 55-2-1: no one may enter land or sue to recover it except within ten years after the right first accrued to that person or to someone through whom they claim. An owner who waits too long to act against an occupant risks letting that clock run. Below is how the doctrine works, how it differs from a tenant who stays after a lease, and what an owner selling a house can do.

Elements an adverse possessor must prove

The West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals lists six elements, and the claimant must prove every one for the full statutory period (Somon v. Murphy Fabrication & Erection Co., 160 W.Va. 84, 232 S.E.2d 524 (1977), repeated in Elder v. Smith (1996)).

  1. The land was held adversely or hostilely.
  2. The possession was actual.
  3. It was open and notorious, sometimes phrased as visible and notorious.
  4. It was exclusive.
  5. It was continuous.
  6. It was under claim of title or color of title.

The period is ten years, and a gap in any element defeats the claim.

The standard of proof is higher than in an ordinary civil case. In Cobb v. Collins (2018), the Court repeated that a party claiming title this way must establish every essential element by clear and convincing evidence, citing Brown v. Brown, 196 W.Va. 559, 474 S.E.2d 489 (1996).

What "hostile" means

Hostile means against the owner's right. It has nothing to do with anger. In Elder v. Smith the Court said the claimant must show possession against the true owner's right and inconsistent with the owner's title, and that hostile is synonymous with adverse and requires no ill will or malevolence.

Permission defeats the element. Someone staying in a relative's house with the owner's consent, or paying rent as a tenant, isn't holding against the owner's right the way the doctrine demands.

When a claimant does meet every element for more than ten years, the syllabus point quoted in Cobb says the result is good legal title, letting that person bring an action for unlawful entry and detainer against anyone who enters unlawfully (Harman v. Alt, 69 W.Va. 287, 71 S.E. 709 (1911)).

Squatter or holdover tenant?

A tenant came in with the owner's permission under a lease or oral arrangement, so the landlord-tenant statutes govern. A squatter came in with no right at all. The remedies differ.

SituationMain legal routeStatute or case
Tenant behind on rent, in breach, or damaging the propertyVerified petition in magistrate or circuit court; hearing 5 to 10 judicial days after filingW. Va. Code 55-3A-1
Occupant claiming title by long possessionAdverse possession doctrine; six elements, ten years, clear and convincing proof55-2-1; Somon; Cobb
Person on property without authority after being asked to leaveCriminal trespass in a structure: misdemeanor, fine up to $10061-3B-2(a)
Entering a structure posted as condemnedMisdemeanor, fine up to $100, jail up to six months, or both61-3B-2(b)

The summary route in Article 3A is written for tenants. It lets a person wanting to remove a tenant apply to the court, and a served tenant may raise any defense available in an ejectment or unlawful detainer action (55-3A-2). Whether an occupant is a tenant, a guest or a trespasser is a question of fact, so get legal advice before acting.

Trespass on a house

Under W. Va. Code 61-3B-2(a), knowingly entering a structure without being authorized or invited, or refusing to leave when the owner, tenant or agent asks, is a misdemeanor with a fine of not more than $100.

Subsection (b) is tougher for condemned buildings. Knowingly and willfully entering a structure clearly posted as condemned by a municipal or county government as unfit for human habitation brings a fine of not more than $100, up to six months in jail, or both. For a first violation the court may substitute community service or pretrial diversion. Subsection (c) adds heavier penalties when the offender is armed with a dangerous weapon and intends bodily injury.

A separate section, 61-3B-3, covers trespass on property other than a structure where notice against entering is given. The details depend on how notice is given, so read that section before posting land.

What an owner should do about an unauthorized occupant

Act early, in writing, and through the proper channel. We aren't lawyers, and the right step depends on whether the person is a tenant, a guest or a stranger. These practical points follow from the statutes above.

  • Write down when you last inspected the house and who had permission to be there.
  • If the person is asked to leave and refuses, the trespass statute turns on a request by the owner, tenant or agent, so keep a record of that request.
  • If the person paid or promised rent, treat it as a tenancy and use the Article 3A petition instead of self-help.
  • Don't wait years. Section 55-2-1 allows ten years for an action to recover land, and continuous possession is one of the elements.
  • Talk to a West Virginia attorney before changing locks, shutting off utilities or removing belongings.

Vacant inherited houses invite these problems. A house sits empty after a death, the owner lives out of state, and months pass between visits. Regular checks, current taxes and a recorded record of who holds title all make it harder for anyone to claim they were there openly and exclusively.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy West Virginia houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How an occupant affects a sale

An occupant changes who can close and how fast. A buyer who plans to live in the house needs possession at closing, and a mortgage buyer's appraiser and inspector need access, which a contested occupant can block.

You can still sell a house with a squatter, a holdover tenant or an unclear occupancy. We buy houses in West Virginia as-is and can discuss an offer where someone is living there without your agreement. We won't tell you the occupant has no rights, and you shouldn't rely on us for that answer. A court decides the title question, and the practical timeline depends on which statute applies.

Before you list or accept an offer, gather the deed, tax bills, any lease, texts or letters with the occupant, and dated photos of the condition. They help whether you evict, negotiate a move-out or sell with the occupant in place.

Frequently asked questions

How long does adverse possession take in West Virginia?

Ten years. W. Va. Code 55-2-1 sets ten years for entering on or recovering land, and the Supreme Court of Appeals names ten years as the statutory period. The claimant must also prove each of the six elements.

What standard of proof applies to an adverse possession claim?

Clear and convincing evidence. In Cobb v. Collins (2018) the Court repeated that the party claiming title this way must prove all essential elements by that standard.

Does a squatter have to be hostile to the owner?

Hostile means possession against the owner's right and inconsistent with the owner's title. The Court said it needs no ill will. Someone with the owner's permission isn't occupying against the owner's right in that sense.

Is trespassing in a house a crime in West Virginia?

Yes. Under 61-3B-2(a), knowingly entering a structure without authorization, or refusing to leave when asked, is a misdemeanor with a fine of not more than $100. Entering a structure posted as condemned carries a higher penalty.

Can I sell my house if someone is living there without permission?

You can sell, but possession is the practical problem. A buyer who needs to move in will want the occupant gone. A cash buyer who purchases as-is may take a house with an occupant, so describe the situation honestly when you ask for an offer.

West Virginia landlord and tenant statutes

Three parts of the West Virginia Code do most of the work: Chapter 37, Article 6 (landlord and tenant), Chapter 37, Article 6A (residential rental security deposits) and Chapter 55, Article 3A (remedies for wrongful occupation of residential rental property). Between them they cover repairs, deposits, notice to end a tenancy and the court route for removing a tenant.

If you own a rental you might sell, these are the rules a buyer steps into. They also decide how quickly a tenant can be moved out when a sale needs an empty house.

  • Article 6 has 31 sections, from transfer of the landlord's interest (37-6-1) to the habitability duty (37-6-30).
  • Article 6A has six sections: definitions, deposits, records, prohibited lease terms, landlord noncompliance and effective date.
  • Article 3A has three sections: the petition, defenses and the court proceeding.

What a sale does to the lease

The lease survives the sale. Under W. Va. Code 37-6-1, a grantee or assignee of leased land, or of the reversion, may use the same conditions, forfeitures and covenants the original lessor could. Section 37-6-2 gives the tenant the matching right: a lessee can enforce the lease's conditions, covenants and promises against whoever takes the reversion, as if that person were the original lessor, except for warranties.

So a signed lease is part of what you are selling. The buyer takes the property subject to the tenant's rights, and the tenant can hold the new owner to the terms.

The deposit goes along too. Under section 37-6A-2(e), whoever owns the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends must follow the deposit rules and return any deposit duly owed. That is true whether or not the deposit changed hands in the sale and regardless of any deal between old and new landlord. If you sell a rental with a tenant in place, settle in writing who carries the deposit, since the tenant can look to the new owner.

Security deposits

When the tenancy ends, within the applicable notice period, the landlord must deliver the deposit less deductions, with a written itemization (37-6A-2(a)). The statute limits what can come out.

Allowed uses under 37-6A-2(b):

  • Rent due, including reasonable late charges stated in the rental agreement.
  • Damage from the tenant's noncompliance with the agreement, less reasonable wear and tear.
  • Unpaid utilities the landlord billed and paid that the tenant owed under the agreement.
  • Reasonable costs to remove and store the tenant's personal property.
  • Other charges named in the agreement, including a third-party contractor's repair of tenant damage.

If damage exceeds the deposit and needs an outside contractor, the landlord gives written notice within the notice period and then has fifteen more days to send the itemization and repair cost (37-6A-2(c)). Handing it over in person works, as does mail to the last known or forwarding address. A mailed deposit that comes back undeliverable is held six months, and the landlord must hand it over within 72 hours of a written request (37-6A-2(g)).

Landlord repair and habitability duties

A residential landlord must deliver the unit fit and habitable and keep it that way (W. Va. Code 37-6-30(a)(1)). The same subsection lists the duties.

  • Meet applicable health, safety, fire and housing codes, unless the tenant, a family member or a guest caused the failure.
  • Keep common areas of multiple housing units clean, safe and in repair.
  • Make repairs needed to keep the premises fit, except those caused mainly by the tenant's lack of reasonable care.
  • Keep electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating and air-conditioning facilities in safe working order when the landlord supplies them.
  • In multiple units, arrange removal of garbage and waste.
  • Where units have direct public utility connections, supply running water, reasonable hot water, and reasonable heat from October 1 through the last day of April.

Two limits apply. A bigger duty written into the rental agreement overrides the statute (37-6-30(b)), and the landlord needn't make repairs while the tenant is behind on rent (37-6-30(c)). Putting off repairs on an occupied unit invites a dispute, and some owners avoid that by selling to a buyer who accepts the place unrepaired.

Removing a tenant through court

Court removal begins with a verified petition, filed in magistrate or circuit court where the property is located (W. Va. Code 55-3A-1). A tenant who outstays the court's date is removed by the sheriff (55-3A-3(f)).

StepWhat happensCitation
PetitionOwner or agent states the right to possession, describes the property and alleges rent arrears, breach of a warranty or lease covenant, or deliberate or negligent damage55-3A-1(a)
Hearing dateCourt sets a hearing not less than five nor more than 10 judicial days after filing55-3A-1(b)
NoticeServed under Rule 4 of the Rules of Civil Procedure or by certified mail, return receipt requested; tenant may file a written defense within five days of receiving it55-3A-1(c)
No responseIf the tenant files nothing by the hearing, the court enters an order granting immediate possession55-3A-3(a)
Contested caseIf the tenant answers, the court holds a hearing; continuances are for cause only, and a tenant who gets one must pay periodic rent into court55-3A-3(d)
OrderCourt sets the vacate time; if the tenant stays, the sheriff removes the tenant55-3A-3(f)

A tenant may raise any defense available in an ejectment or unlawful detainer action (55-3A-2). In a rent case, a tenant who answers that the landlord breached a material covenant on which the duty to pay rent depends gets a hearing on that issue (55-3A-3(b)).

Belongings left behind

After a possession order, the landlord can dispose of property the tenant says in writing is abandoned, or of garbage, without liability (55-3A-3(h)(1)). Otherwise the landlord may remove and store the items or leave them in place, and may dispose of them after thirty days if the tenant hasn't paid reasonable costs or reclaimed them, or if storage costs equal the value of the goods.

Property worth more than $300 that the tenant or a secured party says they plan to collect must be stored up to thirty more days, provided they pay reasonable storage and removal costs (55-3A-3(i)).

A different process fits a tenant who has simply left. Under 37-6-6, if a tenant who owes rent abandons the property, the landlord posts a written notice in a conspicuous place requiring payment within one month. If the rent stays unpaid, the landlord gets possession and the tenant's right ends. Before disposing of belongings, the landlord must post and mail a notice by first-class mail with a certificate of mailing, giving a removal date at least thirty days after mailing (sixty days for a tenant on active military duty who has said so).

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy West Virginia houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

When a landlord keeps the deposit

If a landlord's noncompliance with Article 6A is willful or not in good faith, the tenant is entitled to a judgment for the unreturned deposit plus damages for annoyance or inconvenience of one and a half times the amount wrongfully withheld (37-6A-5(a)). If the tenant owes rent, the court credits the award against it.

The tenant sues in magistrate or circuit court for the rental's county (37-6A-5(b)).

Selling a rental house in West Virginia

These rules set the clock and the cost. A sale with a tenant in place hands the lease, the deposit and the repair duty to the buyer. A sale needing vacant possession means going through the 55-3A court process first, and that requires a valid ground such as unpaid rent or damage.

Owners who sell to us for cash can pick either route. Our as-is purchases include rentals with tenants, and the offer reflects the situation you describe. Before you sign anything, check your lease, your deposit records and any notices you served. If a dispute is open, talk to a West Virginia attorney or see Legal Aid of West Virginia's renters' rights pages. Nothing here is legal advice.

Frequently asked questions

Does a West Virginia tenant have to move out when the landlord sells?

Not because of the sale alone. Under W. Va. Code 37-6-1 and 37-6-2, the buyer takes the landlord's interest subject to the lease, and the tenant can enforce its terms against the new owner. Ending the tenancy still follows the lease and the notice rules.

How long does a landlord have to return a security deposit?

The deposit, less lawful deductions and with a written itemization, is due at termination and within the applicable notice period (37-6A-2(a)). If damage exceeds the deposit and needs a contractor, the landlord gets fifteen more days after written notice to itemize the cost.

Can a landlord cut off heat or lock a tenant out?

The statutes provide a court process for removal (55-3A), with the sheriff enforcing a possession order. Section 37-6-30 also requires reasonable heat from October 1 through April 30 where the landlord supplies it through a direct utility connection. Ask a West Virginia attorney about any specific lockout.

What is the penalty for wrongfully withholding a deposit?

If the noncompliance is willful or not in good faith, the tenant can recover the unreturned deposit plus damages of one and a half times the amount wrongfully withheld (37-6A-5(a)).

Can I sell a rental house with a tenant still living in it?

Yes. The lease and the deposit obligation go with the property, so the buyer steps into the landlord's position. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can take a tenant-occupied house, and you can raise that when you ask for an offer.

How a West Virginia eviction starts

The landlord files a verified petition in the magistrate court or circuit court of the county where the rental sits. Section 55-3A-1 of the West Virginia Code lets an owner or the owner's agent ask for summary relief to remove a tenant from residential rental property.

The petition needs four things: a statement that the petitioner is the owner or agent with a right to recover possession, a short description of the property, the reason the tenant is wrongfully there, and a request for possession. The reason must be one of three: the tenant is behind on rent, has breached a warranty or leasehold covenant, or has deliberately or negligently damaged the property or knowingly let someone else do so. The petition describes the arrearage, breach or act.

The West Virginia Judiciary publishes a petition form titled Petition for Summary Relief, Wrongful Occupation of Residential Rental Property. It cites sections 55-3A-1, 50-5-8(a) and 37-15-3 and Magistrate Court Civil Rule 6A, and it must be sworn or affirmed before a notary.

Notice periods and deadlines

The statute counts hearing and response periods in days, and it ties the no-cause route to the length of the tenancy.

Step or noticeTime periodAuthority
Hearing after petition is filedNot less than 5 and not more than 10 judicial days after filing55-3A-1(b)
Tenant's written defenseWithin 5 days of receiving the notice of hearing55-3A-1(c)
Answer under magistrate rulesWithin 5 days after service of the summons and complaintMagistrate Court Civil Rule 4
Jury demandWritten notice within 5 days of serviceJudiciary petition form
Year-to-year tenancy, termination noticeIn writing, at least three months before the end of any year37-6-5
Periodic tenancy under one year, no-cause noticeNotice for one full period before the end of a period37-6-5
Stored belongings after an orderLandlord may dispose after thirty days in listed cases55-3A-3(h)

Section 55-3A-1 sets no separate pre-filing notice period for the three grounds. A lease with its own notice terms can control, as covered below. If you're unsure which clock applies, call the magistrate court clerk or an attorney before filing.

Ending a tenancy without cause

A landlord can end a month-to-month or other short periodic tenancy by giving notice for one full period before the end of a period. Under section 37-6-5, a year-to-year tenancy ends with written notice from either side at least three months before the end of any year. A periodic tenancy shorter than a year ends by that same notice or by notice for one full period before the end of any period.

Service has rules. A notice meant for the tenant may be served on the tenant or on anyone holding under the tenant, and the same goes for any part of the leased premises. A tenant's notice to the landlord can be served on the owner or the owner's agent.

Two carve-outs apply. The section yields to a special agreement that fixes another notice period or says no notice is due. And no notice is needed for a tenant whose term ends at a certain time.

  • Year to year: written notice at least three months before year end.
  • Shorter periodic tenancy: notice for one full period.
  • Lease with its own terms: check the agreement first.
  • Fixed term ending on a set date: no notice needed under this section.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your West Virginia house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The hearing

The court sets a hearing five to ten judicial days after the petition is filed, and the landlord must serve notice of it right away. Under section 55-3A-1(c), service follows Rule 4 of the West Virginia Rules of Civil Procedure or goes by certified mail, return receipt requested. The notice tells the tenant that a written defense must be filed and served within five days of receipt. The petitioner then files the petition with proof of service.

If the tenant doesn't appear, answer or respond by the hearing, section 55-3A-3(a) directs the court to enter an order granting immediate possession to the landlord. If the tenant answers, the hearing takes up the issues raised. On a rent claim, the tenant can argue the landlord breached a material covenant that the duty to pay rent depends on. On a breach or damage claim, the tenant can raise defenses to the petition. Section 55-3A-2 lets the tenant assert any defense available in an action for ejectment or unlawful detainer.

Continuances are for cause only, never as a matter of right. A tenant who gets one must pay into court any periodic rent that falls due while it lasts.

The order and removal

When the court finds wrongful occupation, it enters an order granting immediate possession and sets the date the tenant must leave. Under section 55-3A-3(f), the court weighs the nature of the property, such as furnished or unfurnished, the possible harm to each side, and other relevant facts in setting that time.

If the tenant stays past the date, the order directs the sheriff to remove the tenant forthwith, taking care to guard against damage to the property of both landlord and tenant. The sheriff does the removal, not the landlord.

On appeal, a winning tenant gets money damages only if the lease term has expired, unless there is an issue of title, retaliatory eviction or breach of warranty. During an appeal, a tenant has no right to stay if the tenancy has otherwise expired.

Belongings left behind

After a possession order, section 55-3A-3(h) gives the landlord three choices for items the tenant leaves. The landlord may dispose of them without liability if the tenant says in writing that they are abandoned or if they are garbage. The landlord may also remove and store them, or leave them on the property.

  • Stored items may be disposed of after thirty days if the tenant hasn't paid reasonable storage and removal costs or taken the property back, or if storage costs equal the value of the items.
  • Items left on the property may be disposed of after thirty days if the tenant hasn't paid the reasonable cost of leaving them or retrieved them.
  • Items worth more than $300 must be stored for up to thirty more days if the tenant or a secured party says they intend to remove them and pays the reasonable costs.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy West Virginia houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a rental with a tenant in it

You can usually sell a rental while it is occupied, but a buyer who wants the house empty has to live with the timeline above. A petition, a hearing five to ten judicial days later, a possible defense, and then a court-set vacate date all come before the sheriff can act.

A conventional buyer who needs a vacant house, or whose lender won't close with an occupant, may walk away from a rental with a pending case. We buy houses as-is, so ask whether an occupied house is something we can take on. Read your lease, and ask a West Virginia attorney whether it binds a new owner.

  • Gather the lease, rent ledger and any written notices.
  • Note whether the tenancy is year to year, periodic or for a fixed term.
  • Photograph any damage before and after the tenant leaves.
  • Keep copies of what you served, and how.

Court forms

The West Virginia Judiciary hosts the petition and a civil summons for wrongful occupation of residential rental property on its magistrate court forms page. The petition form carries a notice that any party seeking over $20.00 or possession of real estate may elect a jury trial, and that in wrongful occupation cases the election must be made in writing within 5 days of service or the right is lost.

Frequently asked questions

How long must a West Virginia landlord wait before filing an eviction?

Section 55-3A-1 sets no separate waiting period for the three grounds: unpaid rent, breach of a warranty or leasehold covenant, and damage to the property. The hearing is set 5 to 10 judicial days after filing. Check your lease for notice terms of its own.

How long does a tenant have to respond to an eviction petition?

Five days. The notice of hearing tells the tenant a written defense may be filed within five days of receipt, and magistrate rules give a defendant 5 days after service of the summons and complaint to answer.

How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy?

Notice for one full period before the end of a period. Under section 37-6-5, a periodic tenancy shorter than a year ends that way, and a year-to-year tenancy needs written notice at least three months before the end of any year. A special agreement in the lease can change this.

Can a landlord remove a tenant without a court order?

No. Under section 55-3A-3, the court's order sets the date to vacate, and if the tenant stays past it the sheriff removes the tenant. Removal is a court and sheriff process.

What happens to a tenant's belongings after an eviction order?

The landlord may dispose of items the tenant has declared abandoned in writing, or garbage. Otherwise the landlord may store the items or leave them in place, and may dispose of them after thirty days in the listed cases. Items worth more than $300 may need up to thirty more days of storage.
